content.user_title: Implement Figma Designs as Production UI
content.value_statement: Design handoff often loses spacing, assets, and component intent. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable Figma MCP workflow for accurate UI implementation.
actual_capabilities: Parses Figma design URLs to identify file keys and node IDs.
Fetches structured design context through the Figma MCP server.
Captures Figma screenshots for visual comparison during implementation.
Uses Figma-provided assets, including icons, images, and SVG files.
Maps Figma tokens and layout data to existing project conventions.
Guides final validation for spacing, typography, color, assets, and accessibility.
limitations: Requires a connected Figma MCP server or selected Figma desktop node.
Requires user access to the target Figma file and selected frame.
Cannot guarantee pixel parity when project design tokens intentionally differ.
Does not replace product review, designer approval, or accessibility testing.

use_cases.title: Build Product Components
use_cases.description: Implement buttons, forms, cards, and other Figma components using existing project patterns.

use_cases.title: Review Design Handoff
use_cases.description: Help developers preserve spacing, typography, colors, assets, and responsive behavior from the source design.

use_cases.title: Create Consistent UI Pages
use_cases.description: Turn dashboard or workflow frames into reusable sections that fit the current application.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Component
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single Figma component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement this Figma component in the current project: [Figma URL]. Use existing components and match the screenshot.

prompt_templates.title: Use Desktop Selection
prompt_templates.scenario: Use a selected node in the Figma desktop app.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the selected Figma desktop node to build the UI. Fetch design context and screenshot before editing files.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Full Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate prompt for a page or dashboard frame.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build this Figma page: [Figma URL]. Break it into sections, reuse project components, and validate responsive behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate a Complex Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for reusable components and design system alignment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this complex Figma flow into reusable project components: [Figma URL]. Map tokens, document deviations, and verify accessibility.

output_examples.input: Implement a Figma button component from a design link.
output: A button variant is added to the existing design system.
Spacing, typography, colors, icons, and states are matched against the screenshot.
The implementation includes a short note about any design token differences.

output_examples.input: Build a dashboard frame from Figma.
output: The dashboard is split into header, sidebar, content, and card sections.
Existing layout primitives and components are reused where available.
The final pass checks responsive behavior, assets, and accessibility.

best_practices: Fetch design context and a screenshot before making implementation decisions.
Reuse existing project components before creating new UI primitives.
Document any visual deviation caused by accessibility or technical constraints.
anti_patterns: Implementing from memory without reading the Figma MCP design context.
Adding new icon packages when Figma already provides the required assets.
Copying raw generated styles without mapping them to project tokens.

faq.question: Does this skill require Figma MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. It depends on Figma MCP or Figma desktop MCP for design context and screenshots.

faq.question: Can it use a selected Figma desktop node?
faq.answer: Yes. With figma-desktop MCP, it can use the currently selected node instead of a URL.

faq.question: Does it generate final code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides the agent through implementation in the current project and its existing conventions.

faq.question: Will it always match Figma exactly?
faq.answer: It aims for close visual parity, but project tokens, accessibility needs, and technical constraints may require changes.

faq.question: Does it add new design system components?
faq.answer: It prefers existing components first. New components are recommended only when no suitable component exists.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with private designs?
faq.answer: Use it only with projects and MCP servers that are authorized to access the target Figma file.
